analysis: What changed vs the 6:00 AM brief: the market opened higher on the cooler PPI monthly print, then faded in the first 25 minutes — SPY slipped from a $760.07 open to $755.22 (-0.25%), and Nvidia's premarket bounce fully reversed, from a $170.00 high to $162.24 (-2.38%). The bounce failing matters more than the open: dip buyers stepped in premarket on the known testimony dates and Wedbush's $345 target, but the stock could not hold the gap, and Reuters' report of a second employee relationship (396 comments on HN) keeps the governance cloud thickening into Tuesday's earnings. The hawkish turn is the other live wire: BofA now forecasts three consecutive hikes (Dec, Jan, Mar), Goldman sees Dec plus March, and Goolsbee said the Fed is 'not on track' for 2% — the 10-year is back above 5.12% and the December hike is priced at 100%, so the relief rally has a rate ceiling. The IEA surplus call is the counterweight: the first oil surplus since the Iran war began undercuts the war premium that lifted crude Thursday, though tanker attacks keep the tail risk alive. Signal vs noise: the PPI monthly cooling and the IEA surplus are real, durable inputs; the NVDA premarket bounce and the Modine premium are noise until earnings and confirmation respectively.

headlines.headline: Stocks opened higher, then faded in the first 25 minutes: Dow +186.86 (+0.36%) to 52,483.95, S&P 500 +21.83 (+0.29%) to 7,614.23, Nasdaq +33.56 (+0.13%) at the open — but SPY has since slipped to $755.22 (-0.25% vs Thursday's $757.12 close) after opening at $760.07.
headlines.why_it_matters: A green open that cannot hold is weaker than a flat open — the PPI relief is being sold into, with the rate-hike repricing capping the bounce.

headlines.headline: Nvidia's premarket bounce fully reversed after the open: NVDA opened at $169.91 (+2.3% vs Thursday's $166.19 close, high $170.00) and has fallen to $162.24 (-2.38%) by ~9:54 AM ET. Wedbush set a $345 price target (Outperform) on Nov 12, and Reuters reported Huang had a relationship with a second employee, sources say.
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce failing at the open shows dip buyers are not yet in control — and a fresh Reuters allegation keeps the governance overhang growing into Tuesday's Nov 17 earnings, Kress's first call as interim CEO.

headlines.headline: Microsoft's 365 outage is into day two with 'early signs of stabilization' but capacity still not back to normal and no confirmed root cause; Microsoft says it is not a cyberattack. MSFT is -0.22% at $521.83 in early trading, recovering from -1.37% premarket ($515.84) and an open of $519.75.
headlines.why_it_matters: Partial recovery is easing the drag, but a second day without a root cause keeps the reliability question open for a stock that was the only Mag 7 name in the red premarket.

headlines.headline: Bank of America now forecasts three consecutive 25bp Fed hikes — December 2026, January 2027 and March 2027 — citing 'borderline disturbing' inflation; Goldman Sachs now sees December plus a third hike in March. Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said the Fed is 'not on track' to hit its 2% target, flagging AI data-center demand as an inflation driver. FedWatch prices a December hike at 100% (87% for 25bp, 13% for 50bp).
headlines.why_it_matters: The hiking path keeps lengthening after hot CPI and PPI — a December hike is now a certainty and the debate is how many follow, which is a headwind for growth multiples while the 10-year sits above 5.1%.

headlines.headline: The IEA's November Oil Market Report says the global oil market returns to surplus in Q4 2026 — the first surplus since the Iran war began — as Gulf exports recover. Global supply rose 2.3 mb/d to 105.4 mb/d in October; North Sea Dated crude is down ~32% from its $136 October peak to ~$93. Brent ~$96.16, WTI ~$89.37 (+0.71%) in early trading.
headlines.why_it_matters: A surplus call undercuts the war premium that lifted crude 2.6% on Thursday — a disinflation tailwind for the tape, though tanker attacks keep the supply risk alive.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split in early trading: AAPL hit a new 52-week high of $360.83 and is +1.40% at $359.85; META +1.57% at $633.37; GOOGL +1.02% at $301.76; AMZN +0.43% at $268.60 — while TSLA faded -1.05% to $393.30 after touching $404.40 at the open.
headlines.why_it_matters: Breadth inside the megacaps is holding up everywhere except the two story stocks (NVDA, TSLA) — the tape is rotating, not breaking.

headlines.headline: Elon Musk's xAI reportedly laid off ~60 employees from its Grok Imagine video-generation team as the company pivots toward AI coding tools and autonomous agents, mirroring recent retrenchment at OpenAI on video-generation costs.
headlines.why_it_matters: Cost discipline is spreading across AI labs — a sentiment check on the AI-spending boom, though xAI is private and the report is single-source, unconfirmed. Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile.
